title: Dry Doddington Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 2 of 7 killed including Sgt. Norman Isaac Langley

external_narratives.summary: 49 Squadron Association memorial page for Lancaster PB432 EA-O at Dry Doddington Church. The aircraft crashed on 26 November 1944 shortly after take-off from Fulbeck for a mission to Munich, laden with bombs and fuel. Two of seven crew killed: Sgt Langley (W/OP) and Sgt Blake (mid-upper gunner).
key_details: Crashed shortly after take-off for Munich raid
Pilot F/O Le Marquand survived with slight injuries

memorial_details:
Name: Blake, E. G.
Location: Avro Lancaster PB432 (WMR 92263) Dry Doddington Lincolnshire
narrative: Lancaster PB432 of 49 Squadron departed Fulbeck on operations on 26 November 1944, with pilot Le Marquand at the controls. The aircraft came down at Dry Doddington, Lincolnshire, a short distance from its home station. Of the seven crew members aboard, two were killed: Sergeant E. G. Blake, air gunner, and Sergeant Norman Isaac Langley, wireless operator. The remaining five, including navigator R.E. Ransom and flight engineer W.S. Wade, survived.
